title: Add initial dissector for Matter
description:
Matter is an interoperable application-layer protocol to control IoT smart
home devices, maintained by the [Connectivity Standards Alliance](https://csa-iot.org/).
The specification can be requested for free at https://csa-iot.org/developer-resource/specifications-download-request/

This dissector currently only parses the outer "message headers"
and the "payload headers" (as long as the payload is not encrypted).
There's also a TLV encoding for the payload,
the application semantics of those TLVs,
encryption, fragmented payloads in UDP, support for TCP, etc.
which is all missing from the dissector for now, so there's still lots to do.
There's stuff I don't even *know* is missing because I didn't get that far reading the spec!

There is no defined port number (implementations pick an arbitrary port and
advertise it over mDNS), so I'm only making Matter available in "Decode As"
for now. In the future it would be nice to get the port from the mDNS
answers.

Some fields in the message header can be encrypted by "message privacy",
and the entire payload can be encrypted too.
Since I don't support decryption yet,
I'm currently skipping those header fields altogether if the "message privacy" flag is set,
and showing `[Encrypted Payload]` if the payload is encrypted.

I welcome nitpicking/bikeshedding on field names, descriptions (naming things hardest problem in computer science etc), code style, or whatever.

notes.body:
I'm attaching a sample capture, UDP-only, produced by running a simulated accessory on my computer using the official SDK, and trying to commission it from my iPhone. The commissioning failed because on iOS, "only the owner of a home, not an invited user, can pair Matter accessories", but it gave me enough packets to start testing anyway. I do not have any corresponding encryption keys.

[matter.pcapng](/uploads/911f70236a27bdd4a9ea98c88a788eb9/matter.pcapng)

I'm working on a Matter dissector as part of my master thesis too. You can set **CHIP_CONFIG_SECURITY_TEST_MODE** and **CHIP_CONFIG_TEST_SHARED_SECRET_VALUE** in CHIPConfig.h to enforce a known shared secret. This (in theory) should make decryption and dissection much easier.

One of the things I noticed right off the bat is the different naming for the flags. We should strive for consistency here, and I would avoid the ".flag."

Yeah that was pretty inconsistent, I kept adding fields and I didn't really read through the whole list again. I now removed the `.flags.` and `flag_*` parts of the field names. Still unsure about some names.

For example, spec says "The Reliability (R) flag is a single bit field which, when set, SHALL indicate that the message sender wishes to receive an acknowledgement for the message". The official SDK code calls it `NeedsAck`. I used `matter.payload.reliability` because by then I had only looked at the spec and not the code. Would `needs_ack` be more readable? Naming is hard :shrug: I guess it would need an opinion from someone who actually works on this protocol...

When in doubt, always go with the specification. It might be useful for users of the official SDK, but for someone analyzing the protocol strictly via the specification, it becomes an issue. I would even go so far and classify this an error in the SDK.
can you add dissector on docbook/release-note... ?

Added. The format in release notes is generally "Long Protocol Name (abbreviation)", but Matter has neither an acronym nor a longer form, so I just used "Matter home automation protocol" ("Matter" alone looked weird, but I have nothing to put in parentheses).

Note that this dissector may be considered too incomplete to even merge for now, but it should be in release notes *when* it's merged, so there it goes :)
Be aware that "[]" is used for generated fields, and this data is not generated.

Strictly speaking, this could be classified as "Matter over WiFi". Not sure if we should make this differentiation, but it is not "Matter over Thread". Communication wise, both should be identical

Strictly speaking it's Matter over UDP, the TCP protocol is slightly different (adds a "packet length" field at the beginning, for example). But I *think* the protocol is exactly the same over WiFi or Thread, so the dissector shouldn't need to worry about that.

I'd need to see a sample Matter-over-Thread capture, and I have 0 hardware supporting Thread...

Stuff like this makes it a little bit hard to review. Stick with one method and go with that. In the case of flags, I would go old-school. Define a flag bitmask and use that here.

Aka
`
#define MESSAGE_FLAG_HAS_SOURCE 0x04
message_flags = message_flags & MESSAGE_FLAG_HAS_SOURCE;
`

You should also try to avoid magic numbers in general and use defines to let them speak. Some magic numbers are ok (aka field lenghts in proto_tree_add_...) but others should be avoided

changed this line in [version 7 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/9865/diffs?diff_id=618358663&start_sha=42a97c48feca2bfd660785654b5af1a5fa7eee38#3508e8a7a10959ae18b39a7d4f7b1eef8625dacb_133_147)

Good suggestion. At first I was a bit reluctant to use `message_has_source = message_flags & MESSAGE_FLAG_HAS_SOURCE` because then its value would be 0 or 4 rather than 0 or 1, and I'd need another macro to say how much to shift, etc. But I realized I don't even need those variables, and it ended up more readable than I expected.
